decisions.title: Rewrite backend/src around the spec's architecture
decisions.context: Existing backend/src is ~450 real lines (mostly transport) plus empty stubs; the spec supersedes its transport, contracts, and layout. No consumer depends on the old ws/patch protocol.
decisions.decision: Adopt the spec's project layout (contracts/socket/coordinator/mastra/services/stores/repositories/fixtures). Delete raw ws, SSE, agent webhook routes, and the stub tree. Salvage zod env validation and tsconfig strictness.
consequences: Old AgentOutput/AgentInput/JsonRenderPatch contracts are retired
Supabase migrations stay on disk but nothing in src references them until persistence is decided
Ingestion parsers (pdf/docx/email, multer) leave src; reintroduce only if the brief requires real document ingestion
alternatives: Adapt existing skeleton and graft Mastra into it

decisions.title: Mastra as the agent runtime
decisions.context: Spec (AI-authored, unapproved) proposed Mastra; team has no prior Mastra experience; hackathon deadline is close. Mastra provides suspend/resume (HITL), memory, and streaming natively.
decisions.decision: Adopt @mastra/core now and validate it inside the engine tracer, where swapping is cheapest. If Mastra fights the tracer, fall back to a plain OpenAI SDK tool loop.
consequences: HITL later rides Mastra tool suspension + manual resumeStream
Pin Mastra versions in the lockfile after the first smoke test (fast-moving API)
Model access goes through ai-sdk provider packages rather than the raw openai client
alternatives: Plain OpenAI SDK v7 hand-rolled loop

decisions.title: Socket.IO as the realtime transport
decisions.context: Run protocol needs per-run rooms, command acknowledgements, idempotency, and reconnect recovery. Repo had raw ws + unmounted SSE; frontend has no realtime client yet, so the choice was free.
decisions.decision: Socket.IO 4.x with rooms run:{runId}, Zod-validated commands with acks, monotonic per-run sequence numbers, connection-state recovery plus an application-level snapshot/event buffer.
consequences: Raw ws and SSE code deleted
Frontend adds socket.io-client
Multi-node scaling would need an adapter later — explicitly out of hackathon scope
alternatives: Keep raw ws and hand-roll rooms/acks/recovery

decisions.title: Engine tracer runs the full slice including json-render
decisions.context: A tracer proves every layer. json-render was an unvalidated AI pick; user chose to validate it inside the tracer rather than defer it.
decisions.decision: Tracer ends at the Next.js frontend rendering a catalog-validated json-render tree via @json-render/react, driven by ui:replace envelopes over socket.io-client.
consequences: Frontend gains socket.io-client and @json-render/react in the tracer
A minimal catalog (few components) ships now; the full spec catalog comes later
If json-render proves unfit, the fallback decision point is immediately after the tracer, before the catalog grows
alternatives: FE debug page with raw JSON feed

decisions.title: The spec is a hypothesis, not a contract
decisions.context: NAUTA_AGENT_BACKEND_SPEC.md was generated by an AI as its initial understanding; the user has not approved or grilled it. The official challenge brief will be shared after the tracer.
decisions.decision: Treat every spec claim as unvalidated until the user or the brief confirms it. Requirements for post-tracer slices are re-derived from the brief, not inherited from the spec.
consequences: Spec acceptance criteria (§22) are NOT the PRD's done-when
Scope beyond the tracer stays open in the PRD
Spec remains the best available architecture reference where the user has endorsed it (D001–D004)
evidence: user message 2026-08-29: spec is 'the initial understanding an AI made, I haven't approved it'

decisions.title: In-memory stores for the tracer; Supabase dormant
decisions.context: Spec defers Postgres; repo carries a complete 276-line Supabase schema plus seed data. Nothing in the tracer needs durability, and a live demo minimizes external failure surface.
decisions.decision: Tracer uses in-memory RunStore/EventStore plus JSON fixtures. Supabase migrations stay in the repo untouched. Persistence is re-decided after the brief arrives.
consequences: Process restart loses runs (documented limitation)
SUPABASE_* env vars become optional in the new config schema
alternatives: Wire Supabase now since the schema exists

decisions.title: OpenAI via ai-sdk provider as the default model path
decisions.context: Existing .env.example carries OpenAI keys; Mastra consumes models through ai-sdk providers. Model ids in the env file (gpt-4o family) are dated.
decisions.decision: Default to @ai-sdk/openai inside Mastra; refresh model ids when wiring the client. Tracer's agent output is deterministic anyway (hello-world tool), so provider risk is near zero at this stage.
consequences: The legacy openai v4 dependency is dropped
Provider swap stays cheap until real reasoning steps land

decisions.title: Use one demo-wide in-memory order incident lifecycle
decisions.context: The stage demo needs a manually triggered order problem to appear immediately in every connected frontend, and the project already uses Socket.IO with in-memory state.
decisions.decision: Raise flexible order incidents through an HTTP API, keep active incidents in backend memory, broadcast lifecycle changes to every connected frontend, replay unacknowledged incidents to reconnecting clients, acknowledge globally, and provide an explicit reset operation.
consequences: Every demo client sees the same active incident set
One client's acknowledgment updates all clients
Backend restart clears incidents
User/workspace targeting and durable persistence remain out of scope
alternatives: Scope incidents to authenticated users or workspaces

decisions.title: Keep order incident demo operations unauthenticated
decisions.context: The user prioritized the fastest happy-path demo and explicitly rejected protection for the manual incident API.
decisions.decision: Raise, acknowledge, and reset operations remain open and unauthenticated for this demo slice.
consequences: Any caller that can reach the backend can create, acknowledge, or clear demo incidents
The feature must be labeled demo-only and is not production-safe
Authentication, authorization, rate limiting, and abuse protection are deferred

decisions.title: Expose a user-safe work trace instead of hidden chain-of-thought
decisions.context: The current chat shows a generic busy state and fabricates a post-hoc step list from rendered component types even though the backend already produces run trace steps. The user wants the work to be inspectable as a beautiful, minimal product surface.
decisions.decision: Treat backend-owned observable work summaries and tool activity as the Work trace. Show real elapsed wall-clock time and these summaries through an accessible collapsed disclosure. Never label inferred component steps, raw provider reasoning, tool payload dumps, or infrastructure logs as the model's complete internal reasoning.
consequences: The frontend must preserve trace metadata per assistant message instead of deriving it from json-render output
The backend remains authoritative for trace steps and total run duration
Existing human-readable tool mappings can power the tracer without a provider migration
Future provider reasoning summaries or live streaming extend the same trace contract rather than changing the UI interface
alternatives: Continue inferring a generic timeline from rendered components
Expose raw tool names, arguments, results, and model reasoning
Migrate models/providers before shipping any trace UI
